newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices rise on speculative buying.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices rise on speculative buying.

text.p: Cotton prices rose on Tuesday, spurred by speculative buying on hopes that the government might authorise further exports of cotton, traders said.
"But mill buying was dull," said a trader.
"We are hopeful the government will allow more exports of cotton in the current season. And this prompted speculative buying," he said.

In spot, Bengal-deshi rose 10 rupees to 910/975 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) and Punjab saw-ginned made similar gains at 1,510/1,675 rupees per maund. Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) rose 200/500 rupees to 12,500/12,700 rupees per candy (355.56 kg). Gujarat Kalyan superior variety was traded steady at 13,000 rupees per candy.
Arrivals were limited and traders were complaining shortage of good quality cotton at the close of the session.
